account_inactive: Account is inactive. Contact your administrator.
account_updated: Your account was updated. Please log in again.
add_new_device_or_media: Add a new device or independent media
assign_examiner_hint: Choose who examines this request. Starting the investigation marks the request received and open.
audit_entry_mismatch: This entry does not match the audit log's record of it: it was changed, replaced or sealed with another key.
audit_entry_not_indexed: This entry is not in the audit log's record. Its change may have failed, or the record was cut.
audit_entry_old_unchanged: An entry from before the audit log was chained. It has not changed since the chain started.
audit_entry_old_unrecorded: An old entry that was not there when the audit log was chained. It may have been added since.
audit_entry_sealed: Audit log entry %s: sealed, in sequence and unchanged.
audit_entry_unreadable: Audit log entry %s is in sequence and unchanged, but its seal can not be opened with the current key.
audit_failed: Not saved: the change could not be recorded in the audit log. Tell an administrator.
audit_report_checkpoint: Audit log when this report was made: entry %s, %s, fingerprint %s.
close_request_devices_not_done: Not closed: some of the request's devices are not done yet.
cumulative_data_from_start_of_year: Cumulative data as gigabytes from the start of the year
edit_strings: Translate or edit the strings, set a new country code to create a new language file. After saving, activate the language file from the settings. Strings that are missing from your language files but are included in the default file are highlighted in red. HTML code and special characters are not supported.
enter_new_to_change: Enter a new password to change.
examination_notes_hidden: Examination notes not shown in report.
examination_notes_shown: Examination notes will be shown in report.
examined_data_as_gb_per_month: Examined data as gigabytes per month
file_notice_file_exists: A file with the same name already exists.
file_notice_file_too_big: The file you are trying to upload is too big.
file_remove_confirm: Are you sure you want to remove attachment?
fill_all_fields_warning: You must fill all the marked fields.
help_access_text: Every user has an access level. Add only users can add requests. View only users can also open requests and read their reports. Investigators edit requests, devices and reports. Administrators also manage users, settings and logs. Once an examiner is assigned, the Access tab of a request can limit it to named users.
help_devices_text: Open the request and go to Devices and medias. Add each item with Add a device or media. Media found inside a device, such as a memory card, SIM card or hard drive, is added under that device. Print a sticker for every device to label it. As the work goes on, move each device's action status from received through to done, and the progress bar of the request follows.
help_intro: Kirjuri keeps track of forensic examination requests, the devices and media that come with them, and how far each examination has got. This page covers the everyday work.
help_licenses_text: Kirjuri is open source software released under the MIT license, and it is built on other open source projects.
help_messages_text: Messages lets users send short notes to each other inside Kirjuri. The number next to it in the menu shows how many are unread.
help_report_text: Write the findings under Examination report. Examination notes are working notes for the examiners and stay out of the report unless you choose to include them. Print report opens the finished report on its own page, ready to print or save as PDF. The case log lists every change made to the request.
help_requests_text: Choose Add a request in the menu and fill in the form. Fields marked with an asterisk are required. The request gets a number made of a running number and the year, and it appears on the front page as new. Requests exported from another Kirjuri can be brought in on the same page from a .krf file.
help_search_text: The search box at the top of the front page finds requests and devices.
help_statuses_text: A request stays new until an examiner presses Start investigation, which makes it open and records the start date. Once every device is done, or marked as no action, broken or empty, the request can be closed as ready, and reopened if more work turns up. Urgent requests carry a lightning bolt, and open requests that have not been updated for a while carry a moon.
help_two_factor_text: With two-factor sign-in, signing in needs your password and a six-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone, so a password alone is not enough. Turn it on under Two-factor sign-in in the menu. Keep the recovery codes you are given: if you lose your phone, each one signs you in once. Codes depend on the clock, so keep your phone's clock set automatically. An administrator can reset two-factor sign-in for a user who has lost both.
https_address_invalid: Saved, except the HTTPS address: write it like https://kirjuri.example.org, without a path.
https_address_other_host: Saved, except the HTTPS address: it must be the address this page is open at. Open Kirjuri there over HTTPS and save it again.
https_needs_https: Saved, except the HTTPS settings: they can only be turned on or changed from this page opened over HTTPS, so that they can not send everyone to an address that does not work.
ip_addr_comma_list: IP addressess or CIDR blocks separated by a comma.
licenses_intro: Kirjuri is released under the MIT license. It includes the software below, each under its own license. Open an entry to read the full license text.
message_or_to_missing: Please specify recipient and message content.
name: Name
new_name_to_create: Add a new username to create a new user.
no_cases: No cases found for the specified year.
no_devices_add_device: No devices. Add a device from the button.
no_search_results: Your search did not return results.
not_in_access_group: You are not in case access group.
not_saved: Not saved. Reload the page and try again.
password_too_short: The password must be at least %d characters long.
pick_examiner: Choose a forensic examiner from the list. If you close this window the request will remain unassigned.
pick_mobile_examiner: Choose a mobile examiner from the list. If the case only contains mobile devices, please choose an appropriate value for the forensic examiner field.
please_relogin: Please log in with your new password
print_sticker_reminder: Remember to print a sticker for every device using the button and return to new case page.
remove_association_warning: Are you sure you want to remove device association for this media?
request_contains_mobile_devices_descr: Request contains mobile devices (tablet devices are considered mobile devices.)
requests_with_matching_complaint_number: Requests with matching criminal complaint number
reservation_in_past: The reservation ends in the past. Check the dates.
search_hint: Searches all years. A word also finds longer words that start with it. Put a phrase in quotes to find it exactly, and a minus sign before a word to leave it out.
search_limited: Only the first %d matches are shown. Add a word to narrow the search.
setting_allow_attachments_help: Allow files to be attached to open requests.
setting_device_action_count_help: The step number of the final status in the device status list (9 in the lists Kirjuri ships). Progress bars are measured against it.
setting_enable_ldap_authentication_help: Let people sign in with their directory account, such as Active Directory, as well as with a Kirjuri account.
setting_fadeout_help: How long the green confirmation message stays on screen, in milliseconds. 20000 is 20 seconds.
setting_hsts_max_age_help: Tells browsers to open Kirjuri only over HTTPS for this long. A browser that has been told will not open Kirjuri at all while HTTPS is broken, such as when the certificate has expired, so try 5 minutes before 1 year. Turn it on from this page opened over HTTPS.
setting_https_address_help: Kirjuri's address over HTTPS, such as https://kirjuri.example.org. Pages opened over plain HTTP move there. Empty leaves plain HTTP as it is. Set it from this page opened at that address over HTTPS.
setting_index_table_condensed_help: Less space between the rows of the front page table, so more requests fit on screen.
setting_lang_help: The language of every page, for every user.
setting_ldap_allowed_netgroups_help: Directory groups whose members may sign in, separated by commas. Empty lets every directory user sign in.
setting_ldap_domain_help: The domain put in front of the username at sign-in, as in DOMAIN\username. Not used when people sign in with name@domain.
setting_ldap_search_string_help: Where in the directory to look up users and their groups, such as dc=example,dc=local.
setting_ldap_server_address_help: Address of the directory server, such as ldaps://dc.example.local. Use ldaps:// so passwords are sent encrypted.
setting_login_max_failures_per_ip_help: Failed sign-ins allowed from one IP address in 15 minutes, whatever usernames were tried. 0 is no limit, for use behind a reverse proxy, where everyone shares its address. Empty is 50.
setting_max_attachment_size_help: Largest file that can be attached, in bytes. The database takes at most 16000000 (16 MB).
setting_motd_help: A notice shown on the sign-in page and at the top of the front page. HTML is allowed. Empty shows nothing.
setting_mysqldump_location_help: Full path of the mysqldump program, which the database backup on this page uses.
setting_notify_after_4_months_help: Mark requests whose confiscation date is over 3 months old on the front page, yellow and then red after 4 months, and highlight the date in the request details after 4 months.
setting_organization_help: Your organization's name, at the top of the case report and in exported .krf files.
setting_organization_specific_prefix_hel: The start of the file number, already filled in on a new request.
setting_phone_number_prefix_help: The start of the investigator's phone number, already filled in on a new request.
setting_progress_bar_style_help: progress-bar for plain device progress bars, progress-bar-striped for striped ones.
setting_report_logo_help: Image at the top of the case report: a path in the Kirjuri folder, such as views/img/logo.png.
setting_report_logo_width_help: Width of the logo on the case report, in pixels.
setting_session_idle_timeout_help: Minutes a sign-in lasts with no Kirjuri page open. An open page keeps it alive. 0 keeps it until the user signs out.
setting_show_errors_help: Show PHP warnings on pages, and error details to administrators. For debugging only: they can reveal file paths.
setting_show_log_help: Show the case log, the list of every change to a request, as a tab of the request.
setting_signature_location_help: Written before the date at the end of the case report, such as In Helsinki.
setting_stalled_case_help: How long an open request can go without an update before it counts as stalled, written like -120 days.
setting_timezone_help: The time zone of the dates and times Kirjuri shows, as a name such as Europe/Helsinki. The database has its own, shown above.
setting_title_text_help: Shown in the browser tab after the name of each page.
setting_two_factor_required_help: Users it applies to set it up at their next sign-in. The anonymous sign-in and API keys are not affected.
subject: Subject
tool_marked_as_inactive: This tool has been marked as inactive and cannot be reserved.
two_factor_blocked: Too many wrong codes have been entered for this account, so codes from the app are refused. Sign in with a recovery code, or ask an administrator to reset two-factor sign-in.
two_factor_blocked_admin: Codes from the app are refused after %d wrong codes in a row. Resetting two-factor sign-in, or bin/kirjuri user:unlock, ends this.
two_factor_blocked_short: Blocked after too many wrong codes
two_factor_enter_code: Open the authenticator app on your phone and enter the six-digit code it shows for Kirjuri.
two_factor_expired: The sign-in took too long. Enter your password again.
two_factor_key_hint: Enter this key in the app instead, as a time-based key:
two_factor_ldap_confirm: Your account signs in through the domain, so changes here need a sign-in within the last ten minutes. If this is refused, sign out and in again first.
two_factor_new_codes_confirm: Make new recovery codes? Your old ones will stop working.
two_factor_new_codes_hint: New codes replace the old ones, which stop working.
two_factor_qr_label: QR code to scan with your authenticator app
two_factor_recovery_codes_intro: If you lose your phone, sign in with one of these codes instead. Each works once. Print them or write them down, and keep them somewhere safe, away from your phone. They are shown only now.
two_factor_recovery_used: You signed in with a recovery code; %d left. If you lost your phone, set up two-factor sign-in on your new one.
two_factor_required_for_you: Two-factor sign-in is required for your account, so it can not be turned off.
two_factor_set_up_again: Set up on a new phone
two_factor_set_up_again_hint: Your current app keeps working until you finish here. Then it stops working, and so do your old recovery codes.
two_factor_setup_required: Your administrator requires two-factor sign-in. Set it up now to sign in.
two_factor_sign_in_again: For your security, sign out and in again, then make this change within ten minutes.
two_factor_status_off: Your password alone signs you in. Turn on two-factor sign-in so that someone who learns your password still can not sign in without your phone.
two_factor_status_on: Signing in needs your password and a code from the authenticator app on your phone.
two_factor_step_code: Enter the six-digit code the app shows
two_factor_step_install: Install an authenticator app on your phone if it does not have one, for example Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, FreeOTP or Aegis.
two_factor_step_scan: In the app, add an account and scan this code.
two_factor_throttled: Too many failed sign-ins. Wait 15 minutes and try again.
two_factor_turn_off_confirm: Turn off two-factor sign-in? Your password alone will then sign you in.
two_factor_turn_off_hint: Your password alone will sign you in again.
two_factor_unavailable: Codes can not be checked at the moment, as the server is missing its two-factor key. Sign in with a recovery code, or ask an administrator.
two_factor_use_recovery_code: Lost your phone? Use a recovery code
two_factor_wrong_code: That code is not right. Enter the newest code from the app. If codes keep failing, check that the clock on your phone is set automatically.
two_factor_wrong_codes_warning: %d wrong two-factor codes were entered for your account since you last signed in. If that was not you, someone knows your password: change it now.
two_factor_wrong_recovery_code: That recovery code is not right, or it has been used already.
